1. Inner joins

1. Joining tables

A join combines rows from two tables. The ON clause gives the join constraint that decides which row pairs match.

1.1. INNER JOIN

An INNER JOIN keeps only the row pairs that satisfy the join constraint. Rows without a partner in the other table are dropped from the result.

SELECT c.name, o.id
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

1.2. LEFT JOIN

A LEFT JOIN, also called a LEFT OUTER JOIN, keeps every row of the left table. When no row of the right table matches, the columns of the right table are NULL in the result.

Adding WHERE o.id IS NULL after a left outer join keeps only the left rows that have no match at all.
